verses.zh: 约西亚登基的时候年八岁，在耶路撒冷作王三十一年。
verses.en: Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned for thirty-one years in Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
verses.commentary:
34:1 "eight years old" There are several time designators in this chapter.

- eight years old, v. 1

- in the eighth year of his reign, v. 3

- in the twelfth year of his reign, v. 3

- in the eighteenth year of his reign, v. 8

SPECIAL TOPIC: KINGS OF THE DIVIDED KINGDOM

The IVP Bible Background Commentary (OT), p. 457, puts Josiah's reign (640-609 b.c.) in historical context.

- At the death of Ashurbanipal (669-603 b.c.), the Assyrian Empire began to lose power and control of the ANE.

- By Josiah's time, two Egyptian Pharaoh's impacted Judah.

- Psammetichus I (Psamtik, 663-609 b.c.)

- Neco II (609-593 b.c.); the one who passed through Judah to fight Assyria and in the conflict Josiah is fatally wounded
(for a good brief note on the tragedy of Josiah's death, see Hard Sayings of the Bible, pp. 245-246)

- In the rising power of Neo-Babylon, Nabopolassar (626-605 b.c.) was in control.

CHART: A BRIEF HISTORICAL SURVEY OF THE POWERS OF MESOPOTAMIA (using dates primarily from
John Bright's A History of Israel, p. 462ff)

verses.zh: 他行耶和华眼中看为正的事，效法他祖大卫所行的，不偏左右。
verses.en: He did what the Lord approved[NOTE:1] and followed in his ancestor David’s footsteps;[NOTE:2] he did not deviate to the right or the left.
notes: Heb “he did what was proper in the eyes of the Lord.”
Heb “and walked in the ways of David his father.”
verses.commentary:
34:2 Notice how Josiah's reign is characterized.

- He did right in the sight of the Lord.

- He walked in the ways of his father David.

- He did not turn aside to the right or left (this idiom denotes conformity to God's revealed laws,
cf. Deut. 5:32; 17:11,20; 28:14; Josh. 1:7; 23:6; Pro. 25:25-27; 2 Kgs. 22:2).

The Chronicler spends much of his writings on David, Solomon, Asa, Jehoshaphat, Hezekiah, and Josiah.
These kings demonstrated the power of obedience and devotion. Their lives were to be emulated by post-exilic Judah.

verses.zh: 他作王第八年，尚且年幼，就寻求他祖大卫的　神。到了十二年才洁净犹大和耶路撒冷，除掉邱坛、木偶、雕刻的像，和铸造的像。
verses.en: In the eighth year of his reign, while he was still young, he began to seek the God of his ancestor[NOTE:1] David. In his twelfth year he began ridding[NOTE:2] Judah and Jerusalem of the high places, Asherah poles, idols, and images.
notes: Heb “father.”
Heb “purifying.”
verses.commentary:
34:3 Josiah's personal faith developed early.

- He began to seek the God of his father, David; see full note on VERB at 2 Chr. 7:14 (eighth year, v. 3).

- He began to purge Judah and Jerusalem of idolatry (twelfth year, vv. 3-7).

- he destroyed high places, vv. 3,4,7

- he destroyed Asherim, vv. 3-4,7

- he destroyed the carved images, vv. 3-4

- he destroyed the molten images, vv. 3-4

- he destroyed the incense altars, vv. 4,7

- he desecrated the graves of idol worshipers, v. 4

- he desecrated the bones of the pagan priests on their altars, v. 5 (cf. 1 Kings 13)

None of the previous attempts at spiritual reform worked (i.e., 2 Chr. 14:5; 15:17; 17:6; 20:37; 33:15-17).
The people of God had become completely and irreversibly entangled with Canaanite fertility worship. The Assyrian and
Babylonian exiles were YHWH's drastic measures to restore pure worship. They were an act of His love, as well as an act of
His judgment.

SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL'S MANDATED RESPONSE TO CANAANITE FERTILITY WORSHIP

verses.zh: 众人在他面前拆毁巴力的坛，砍断坛上高高的日像，又把木偶和雕刻的像，并铸造的像打碎成灰，撒在祭偶像人的坟上，
verses.en: He ordered the altars of the Baals to be torn down[NOTE:1] and broke the incense altars that were above them. He smashed the Asherah poles, idols, and images, crushed them, and sprinkled the dust over the tombs of those who had sacrificed to them.
notes: Heb “and they tore down before him the altars of the Baals.”
verses.commentary:
34:4 "incense altars" In the past the Hebrew word (BDB 329) was translated "son-pillars" (i.e., BDB 329;
John Joseph Owens, Analytical Key to the OT, p. 921, and Rotherham's Emphasized Bible, p. 465.
However, modern archaeology says that this term means "incense altar" (cf. Lev. 26:30; 2 Chr. 14:5; 34:4,7; Isa. 17:8; 27:9).
R. K. Harrison, Old Testament Times, p, 8, discusses this archaeological find from Palmyra, northern Syria,
found on a horned limestone altar.

I like R. K. Harrison so much because he relates the OT to the ANE. Two other persons I trust who do
the same thing are

- John H. Walton, Ancient Israelite Literature in Its Cultural Context and The Lost World of Genesis One: Ancient
Cosmology and the Origins Debate and Ancient Near Eastern Thought and the OT: Introducing the Conceptual World of the
Hebrew Bible

- D. Brent Sandy, Plowshares and Pruning Hooks: Rethinking the Language of Biblical Prophecy and Apocalyptic

- together, #1 and #2 wrote, The Lost World of Scripture: Ancient Literary Culture and Biblical Authority

I highly recommend all three authors who take the historical and literary setting of Scripture seriously!

verses.zh: 将他们祭司的骸骨烧在坛上，洁净了犹大和耶路撒冷；
verses.en: He burned the bones of the pagan priests[NOTE:1] on their altars; he purified Judah and Jerusalem.
notes: Heb “the priests”; the qualifying adjective “pagan” has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 又在玛拿西、以法莲、西缅、拿弗他利各城，和四围破坏之处，都这样行；
verses.en: In the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, and Simeon, as far as Naphtali, and in the ruins[NOTE:1] around them,
notes: “In their ruins” is the marginal reading (Qere) of the Hebrew text.
verses.commentary:
34:6 The northern kingdom had been defeated and exiled to Assyria since 722 b.c. (Manasseh's reign). Josiah
extends his purge and reform to the northern tribes.

The "remnant of Israel" is mentioned in 2 Chr. 34:9.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE REMNANT, THREE SENSES

"Simeon" It is surprising that the tribe of Simeon is mentioned here. Simeon was incorporated into Judah very early.
Simeon is not mentioned at all in Samuel and Kings. It is mentioned briefly in lists in 1 Chronicles (cf. 1 Chr. 2:1; 4:24,42; 6:65;
12:25). It is mentioned only twice in 2 Chronicles, both in connection with reforms (i.e., Asa's, 2 Chr. 15:9 and Josiah's, 2 Chr. 34:9).

NASB
"in their surrounding ruins"

NKJV
"and all around, with axes"

NRSV
"in their ruins all around"

TEV
"and the devastated areas"

NJB
"and around their open spaces"

JPSOA
"(lying) in ruins on every side"

REB
"he burnt down their houses wherever he found them"

LXX
"in reference to their sites round about"

Peshitta
"in their streets round about"

Rotherham's Bible
"searched their houses round about"

MT Ketiv has "he chose their houses"; the Qere has "with their swords" or "in their ruins."
The UBS Text Project, p. 484, gives the MT a "C" rating (considerable doubt).

The context is Josiah's destruction of idols and idol worship. Apparently this different phrase refers to a
search for these abominations in public (i.e., in the square, NJB) and private homes (i.e., REB, Rotherham's Bible). Josephus,
Antiq. 10.4.5., mentions this house-to-house search for idols.

Martin J. Selman, Tyndale OT Commentaries, p. 529, suggests the phrase means "destroyed their
temples," following I. Seeligmann.

verses.zh: 又拆毁祭坛，把木偶和雕刻的像打碎成灰，砍断以色列遍地所有的日像，就回耶路撒冷去了。
verses.en: he tore down the altars and Asherah poles, demolished the idols, and smashed all the incense altars throughout the land of Israel. Then he returned to Jerusalem.

verses.zh: 约西亚王十八年，净地净殿之后，就差遣亚萨利雅的儿子沙番、邑宰玛西雅、约哈斯的儿子史官约亚去修理耶和华―他　神的殿。
verses.en: In the eighteenth year of his reign, he continued his policy of purifying the land and the temple.[NOTE:1] He sent Shaphan son of Azaliah, Maaseiah the city official, and Joah son of Joahaz the secretary to repair the temple of the Lord his God.
notes: Heb “to purify the land and the house.”
verses.commentary:
34:8-13 These verses document Josiah's temple repair. Obviously the temple had been neglected and its procedures
forgotten or ignored.

The repair was done by the supervision of Levites, using non-Levite workers. This fits the Chronicler's interest
and affirmation of the Levites (cf. 2 Kgs. 22:7).

verses.zh: 他们就去见大祭司希勒家，将奉到　神殿的银子交给他；这银子是看守殿门的利未人从玛拿西、以法莲，和一切以色列剩下的人，以及犹大、便雅悯众人，并耶路撒冷的居民收来的。
verses.en: They went to Hilkiah the high priest and gave him the silver that had been brought to God’s temple. The Levites who guarded the door had collected it from the people of[NOTE:1] Manasseh and Ephraim and from all who were left in Israel, as well as from all the people of[NOTE:2] Judah and Benjamin and the residents of[NOTE:3] Jerusalem.
notes: Heb “from Manasseh and Ephraim.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the names “Manasseh and Ephraim” here by metonymy for the people of Manasseh and Ephraim.

Heb “all Judah and Benjamin.” The words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity. The Hebrew text uses the names “Judah and Benjamin” here by metonymy for the people of Judah and Benjamin.
The Hebrew consonantal text (Kethib) assumes the reading, “and the residents of.” The marginal reading (Qere) is “and they returned.”

verses.zh: 又将这银子交给耶和华殿里督工的，转交修理耶和华殿的工匠，
verses.en: They handed it over to the construction foremen[NOTE:1] assigned to the Lord’s temple. They in turn paid the temple workers to restore and repair it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “doer[s] of the work.”
Heb “and they gave it to the doers of the work who were working in the house of the Lord to restore and to repair the house.”

verses.zh: 就是交给木匠、石匠，买凿成的石头和架木与栋梁，修犹大王所毁坏的殿。
verses.en: They gave money to the craftsmen and builders to buy chiseled stone and wood for the braces and rafters of the buildings that the kings of Judah had allowed to fall into disrepair.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “of the houses that the kings of Judah had destroyed.”

verses.zh: 这些人办事诚实，督工的是利未人米拉利的子孙雅哈、俄巴底；督催的是哥辖的子孙撒迦利亚、米书兰；还有善于作乐的利未人。
verses.en: The men worked faithfully. Their supervisors were Jahath and Obadiah (Levites descended from Merari), as well as Zechariah and Meshullam (descendants of Kohath). The Levites, all of whom were skilled musicians,
verses.commentary:
34:12-13 Once again, the Chronicler highlights the ministry of the Levites. These families of the tribe of Levi, given by
YHWH to help the priests, are mentioned mostly in the books of

- Numbers (56 times)

- 1 Chronicles (34 times)

- 2 Chronicles (64 times)

- Ezra ‒ Nehemiah (59 times)

It is surprising that the Chronicler does not mention the Levites' faithfulness, as does 2 Kgs. 22:7
(also note 2 Chr. 12:15).

Apparently the Levite musicians set a tempo for the construction crew (see the Jerome Biblical
Commentary, I, p. 425).

verses.zh: 他们又监管扛抬的人，督催一切做工的。利未人中也有作书记、作司事、作守门的。
verses.en: supervised the laborers and all the foremen on their various jobs.[NOTE:1] Some of the Levites were scribes, officials, and guards.
notes: Heb “[were] over the laborers and were directing every doer of work for work assignment and work assignment.”

verses.zh: 他们将奉到耶和华殿的银子运出来的时候，祭司希勒家偶然得了摩西所传耶和华的律法书。
verses.en: When they took out the silver that had been brought to the Lord’s temple, Hilkiah the priest found the law scroll the Lord had given to Moses.
verses.commentary:
34:14-21 These verses document the wonderful discovery of "the book of the law of the
Lord given by Moses." It is uncertain to what Scriptures this refers.

- Genesis ‒ Deuteronomy

- Deuteronomy (esp. chapter 28)

- part of Exodus (i.e., the Book of the Covenant, v. 30, cf. Exodus 19-24)

- Leviticus (esp. chapter 26)

Josephus, Antiq. 10.4.2., says "the holy books of Moses"; notice the PLURAL.

Notice the levels of royal leadership.

- the High Priest ‒ Hilkiah

- the royal recorder ‒ Shaphan

- the royal servant ‒ Asaiah

- the prophetess ‒ Huldah

SPECIAL TOPIC: MOSES' AUTHORSHIP OF THE PENTATEUCH

34:14 YHWH's codified revelation to Moses is called by several names in Chronicles and Ezra ‒ Nehemiah
(note the variety).

- "the Law of the Lord ‒ 1 Chr. 16:40; 2 Chr. 12:1; 31:3,4; 35:26; Ezra 7:10

- "the Law of the Lord your God" ‒ 1 Chr. 22:12

- "My Law" ‒ 2 Chr. 6:16

- "the Law and the commandment" ‒ 2 Chr. 14:4; 31:21

- "the book of the Law of the Lord" ‒ 2 Chr. 17:9; 34:14

- "between Law and commandment, statutes and ordinances" ‒ 2 Chr. 19:10

- "the law of Moses" ‒ 2 Chr. 23:18; 30:16; Ezra 3:2; 7:6

- "in the Law in the book of Moses" ‒ 2 Chr. 25:4

- "according to the whole Law, the statutes and the ordinances" ‒ 2 Chr. 33:8

- "the book of the law" ‒ 2 Chr. 34:15

- "of the Law" ‒ 2 Chr. 34:19

- "the book of the covenant" ‒ 2 Chr. 34:30

- "His commandments and His testimonies and His statutes" ‒ 2 Chr. 34:31

- "the commandment of our God. . .according to the Law" ‒ Ezra 10:3

- "the book of the Law of Moses" ‒ Neh. 8:1

- "the law" ‒ Neh. 8:2,7,14

- "the book of the law" ‒ Neh. 8:3

- "from the book, from the law of God" ‒ Neh. 8:8

- "the words of the law" ‒ Neh. 8:9,13

- "the book of the law of God" ‒ Neh. 8:18

- "the book of the law of the Lord their God" ‒ Neh. 9:3

- "just ordinances and true laws, good statutes and commandments" ‒ Neh. 9:13,14

- "Your Law" ‒ Neh. 9:26,29,34

- "the Law of God" ‒ Neh. 10:28

verses.zh: 希勒家对书记沙番说：「我在耶和华殿里得了律法书。」遂将书递给沙番。
verses.en: Hilkiah informed Shaphan the scribe, “I found the law scroll in the Lord’s temple.” Hilkiah gave the scroll to Shaphan.
verses.commentary:
34:15 "the scribes" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SCRIBES.

verses.zh: 沙番把书拿到王那里，回覆王说：「凡交给仆人们办的都办理了。
verses.en: Shaphan brought the scroll to the king and reported,[NOTE:1] “Your servants are doing everything assigned to them.
notes: Heb “returned still the king a word, saying.”

verses.zh: 耶和华殿里的银子倒出来，交给督工的和匠人的手里了。」
verses.en: They melted down the silver in the Lord’s temple[NOTE:1] and handed it over to the supervisors and the construction foremen.”
notes: Heb “that was found in the house of the Lord.”

verses.zh: 书记沙番又对王说：「祭司希勒家递给我一卷书。」沙番就在王面前读那书。
verses.en: Then Shaphan the scribe told the king, “Hilkiah the priest has given me a scroll.” Shaphan read it out loud before the king.
verses.commentary:
34:18 The recently found book was read to Josiah. This was part of YHWH's guidelines for the king
(cf. Deut. 17:19) and the people (cf. Exod. 24:7; Deut. 4:9-10; 31:11). Reading of the Law of Moses to the people
was also part of the covenant renewal ceremony (cf. Josh. 8:30-35; Nehemiah 8; 9:3).

verses.zh: 王听见律法上的话，就撕裂衣服，
verses.en: When the king heard the words of the law, he tore his clothes.
verses.commentary:
34:19 "he tore his clothes" This was a sign of mourning.

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

verses.zh: 吩咐希勒家与沙番的儿子亚希甘、米迦的儿子亚比顿、书记沙番，和王的臣仆亚撒雅说：
verses.en: The king ordered Hilkiah, Ahikam son of Shaphan, Abdon son of Micah,[NOTE:1] Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah the king’s servant,
notes: The parallel account in 2 Kgs 22:12 has the variant spelling “Achbor son of Micaiah.”

verses.zh: 「你们去为我、为以色列和犹大剩下的人，以这书上的话求问耶和华；因我们列祖没有遵守耶和华的言语，没有照这书上所记的去行，耶和华的烈怒就倒在我们身上。」
verses.en: “Go, ask the Lord[NOTE:1] for me and for those who remain in Israel and Judah about the words of this scroll that has been discovered. For the Lord’s great fury has been ignited[NOTE:2] against us because our ancestors did not obey the word of the Lord by living[NOTE:3] according to all that is written in this scroll.”
notes: The implication is to seek a prophetic oracle.
The MT reads נִתְּכָה (nittekah, “has gushed forth”) but the LXX implies נִצְתָה (nitsetah, “has been ignited”).
Heb “doing.”
verses.commentary:
34:21 This verse clearly shows why Josiah was grieving. It was the people of God's covenant disobedience
which triggered His judgment (cf. Leviticus 26; Deuteronomy 28).

verses.zh: 于是，希勒家和王所派的众人都去见女先知户勒大。户勒大是掌管礼服沙龙的妻，沙龙是哈斯拉的孙子、特瓦的儿子。户勒大住在耶路撒冷第二区；他们请问于她。
verses.en: So Hilkiah and the others sent by the king[NOTE:1] went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum son of Tokhath, the son of Hasrah,[NOTE:2] the supervisor of the wardrobe.[NOTE:3] (She lived in Jerusalem in the Mishneh[NOTE:4] district.) They stated their business,[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “and those who [were sent by] the king.”
The parallel account in 2 Kgs 22:14 has the variant spelling “son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas.”
Heb “the keeper of the clothes.”
Or “second.” For a discussion of the possible location of this district, see M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 283.
Heb “and they spoke to her like this.”
verses.commentary:
34:22-28 Josiah commanded the priests (i.e., "go," "inquire," Qal IMPERATIVES) to find a
prophet to give clear guidance on what he should do. They went to Huldah the prophetess, not Jeremiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

Her words were very strong about YHWH's plans to judge His people because of their repeated idolatry and
faithlessness, both leaders and people. The curses of the law have been loosed (cf. 2 Chr. 34:24-25)! This, however, will
not happen in Josiah's day. He will have a reign of peace (v. 28).

Notice the words of the prophetess, as well as prophets, reinforce the written word, not add to it. They are
interpreters of revelation, not innovators.

SPECIAL TOPIC: PROPHETS (OT)

verses.zh: 她对他们说：「耶和华―以色列的　神如此说：『你们可以回覆那差遣你们来见我的人说，
verses.en: and she said to them: “This is what the Lord God of Israel says: ‘Say this to the man who sent you to me:

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：我必照着在犹大王面前所读那书上的一切咒诅，降祸与这地和其上的居民；
verses.en: “This is what the Lord says: ‘I am about to bring disaster on this place and its residents, all the curses that are recorded in the scroll which they read before the king of Judah.

verses.zh: 因为他们离弃我，向别神烧香，用他们手所做的惹我发怒，所以我的忿怒如火倒在这地上，总不熄灭。』
verses.en: This will happen because they have abandoned me and offered sacrifices[NOTE:1] to other gods, angering me with all the idols they have made.[NOTE:2] My anger will ignite against this place and will not be extinguished!’”
notes: Or “burned incense.”

Heb “angering me with all the work of their hands.” The present translation assumes this refers to idols they have manufactured (note the preceding reference to “other gods”). However, it is possible that this is a general reference to their sinful practices, in which case one might translate, “angering me by all the things they do.”
verses.commentary:
34:25 "all the works of their hands" This refers to the creation of idols, either

- carved and overlaid

- molten metal formed into idols

"provoke Me to anger. . .My wrath" See

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANTHROPOMORPHIC LANGUAGE USED TO DESCRIBE GOD.

verses.zh: 然而差遣你们来求问耶和华的犹大王，你们要这样回覆他说：『耶和华―以色列的　神如此说：至于你所听见的话，
verses.en: Say this to the king of Judah, who sent you to seek an oracle from the Lord: “This is what the Lord God of Israel says concerning the words you have heard:

verses.zh: 就是听见我指着这地和其上居民所说的话，你便心里敬服，在我面前自卑，撕裂衣服，向我哭泣，因此我应允了你。这是我―耶和华说的。
verses.en: ‘You displayed a sensitive spirit[NOTE:1] and humbled yourself before God when you heard his words concerning this place and its residents. You humbled yourself before me, tore your clothes, and wept before me, and I have heard you,’ says the Lord.
notes: Heb “Because your heart was tender.”
verses.commentary:
34:27 Josiah and the people will be spared YHWH's wrath because

- Josiah's heart was tender (BDB 939, KB 1236, Qal PERFECT)

- Josiah humbled himself before God (BDB 488, KB 484, Niphal IMPERFECT with waw,
cf. 1 Chr. 28:9; 2 Chr. 7:14; 12:7; 32:26)

- tore his clothes, 2 Chr. 34:19

- wept before Me (i.e., in prayer)

SPECIAL TOPIC: GRIEVING RITES

NASB, NKJV
"your heart was tender"

NRSV
"your heart was penitent"

TEV
"you repented"

NJB
"your heart has been touched"

JPSOA
"your heart was softened"

REB
"you have shown a willing heart"

LXX
"your heart was embarrassed"

is used in two senses.

- fear of men ‒ Deut. 20:3,8

- soft hearted towards God ‒ 2 Kgs. 22:19; 2 Chr. 12:7; 32:26

verses.zh: 我必使你平平安安地归到坟墓，到你列祖那里，我要降与这地和其上居民的一切灾祸，你也不致亲眼看见。』」他们就回覆王去了。
verses.en: ‘Therefore I will allow you to die and be buried in peace.[NOTE:1] You will not have to witness all the disaster I will bring on this place and its residents.’”’” Then they reported back to the king.
notes: Heb “Therefore, behold, I am gathering you to your fathers, and you will be gathered to your tomb in peace.”

verses.zh: 王差遣人招聚犹大和耶路撒冷的众长老来。
verses.en: The king summoned all the leaders of Judah and Jerusalem.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the king sent and gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.”
verses.commentary:
34:29-33 This is a covenant renewal ceremony.

- law is read

- people promised (INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT, Qal)

- to walk after YHWH, 2 Chr. 34:31

- to keep His law, v. 31

- to perform the words of the book, v. 31

verses.zh: 王和犹大众人，与耶路撒冷的居民，并祭司利未人，以及所有的百姓，无论大小，都一同上到耶和华的殿；王就把殿里所得的约书念给他们听。

verses.en: Josiah removed all the detestable idols from all the areas belonging to the Israelites and encouraged[NOTE:1] all who were in Israel to worship the Lord their God. Throughout the rest of his reign[NOTE:2] they did not turn aside from following the Lord God of their ancestors.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own
interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of
the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What makes Judean kings do what is right in YHWH's eyes?

- What did Josiah do to the idols in the land?

- What was "the book of the law of the Lord"?

- Why did Josiah tear his clothes when he heard the law read?

- What does 2 Chr. 34:22 say about female leadership?

- What are "the curses" of the book in 2 Chr. 34:24?

- Why did YHWH delay His judgment?

- How can 2 Chr. 34:28 be reconciled with Josiah's early, violent death in chapter 35?

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: 34:1-7

1Josiah was eight years old when he became king, and he reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem.
2He did right in the sight of the Lord, and walked in the ways of his
father David and did not turn aside to the right or to the left. 3For in the eighth year of his reign while
he was still a youth, he began to seek the God of his father David; and in the twelfth year he began to purge Judah
and Jerusalem of the high places, the Asherim, the carved images and the molten images. 4They
tore down the altars of the Baals in his presence, and the incense altars that were high above them he chopped
down; also the Asherim, the carved images and the molten images he broke in pieces and ground to powder and
scattered it on the graves of those who had sacrificed to them. 5Then he burned the bones of the
priests on their altars and purged Judah and Jerusalem. 6In the cities of Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon,
even as far as Naphtali, in their surrounding ruins, 7he also tore down the altars and beat the Asherim
and the carved images into powder, and chopped down all the incense altars throughout the land of Israel. Then
he returned to Jerusalem.
